context: Every date column in financial.sqlite (account.date, loan.date, client.birth_date, card.issued, trans.date) is TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'. The evidence names the domain mapping but never the dialect (suite/families/text2sql.py:22), so a general model reaches for YEAR() or DATE_FORMAT and fails on first contact.
counterfactual: The overshoot is a dialect the database does not speak: YEAR(T1.date) = 1997 raises 'no such function: YEAR', which the check at suite/families/text2sql.py:214 reads as a failed task, and a pass that then repairs it has spent a second call it does not have under text2sql-strict. The opposite overshoot is over-formatting - wrapping an already-ISO literal in DATE() adds nothing.
decision: Dates in financial.sqlite are TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'. A year is STRFTIME('%Y', col) = '1997' (a quoted string, never the integer 1997); a month is STRFTIME('%m', col) = '03'; a range is col BETWEEN '1995-01-01' AND '1997-12-31' (inclusive, ISO literals); an exact day is col = '1976-01-29' - rewrite '1976/1/29' or '1/29/1976' to zero-padded ISO before comparing. 'Account opening date' is account.date, 'loan approved date' is loan.date, 'born' is client.birth_date, 'oldest' is ORDER BY birth_date ASC. Never YEAR(), MONTH(), EXTRACT, DATE_FORMAT or DATEPART: SQLite has none of them and the error fails the task.

residue: whether the pass chose the right date column (opening vs approval) is judgment; the floor checks shape only

options.name: A — STRFTIME and ISO string literals
options.why: the only date functions SQLite has; string comparison on 'YYYY-MM-DD' text sorts chronologically

options.name: B — YEAR(), EXTRACT, DATE_FORMAT
options.why: MySQL/Postgres functions; SQLite raises 'no such function' and the check reads the raise as a failed task
